nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the main purpose of the study on AI applications in retrofit projects?
nodes.answer: The main purpose of the study is to review AI applications and techniques used in retrofit projects, evaluate their impact on overcoming complexities in retrofit scenarios, and identify key datasets and outcomes associated with these applications.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_001
nodes.label: Research Methodology
nodes.question: What methodology was employed to conduct the review of AI applications for retrofit processes?
nodes.answer: The review was conducted using the PRISMA technique, which focuses on improving the reporting of systematic reviews and meta-analyses, combined with a mixed-method literature review involving qualitative analysis and thematic analysis of AI subfields related to retrofit.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What methodology was used in the research to review AI applications for retrofit projects?
nodes.answer: The research employed the PRISMA technique for systematic reviews and meta-analyses, alongside a mixed-method literature review comprising qualitative systematic review and thematic analysis.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What methodology did the study employ to analyze the literature on AI applications for retrofit?
nodes.answer: The study employed a mixed-method literature review using the PRISMA technique, which included a qualitative systematic review and thematic analysis of subfields related to AI for Retrofit.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What methodology was utilized in the study to review AI applications for retrofitting?
nodes.answer: The study employed a mixed-method literature review utilizing the PRISMA technique, which includes a qualitative systematic review and thematic analysis of subfields related to AI for retrofit, conducted in several stages including publication search and data cleansing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_005
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What challenges associated with AI applications in retrofit projects does the study highlight?
nodes.answer: The study highlights several challenges that prevent the wide use of AI in retrofit projects, including cultural barriers, lack of skills, high start-up costs for AI solutions, a shortage of talent, security concerns, limited computer capacity, and poor internet access.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which technique was employed for conducting the review of AI applications for retrofit processes?
nodes.answer: The review was conducted using the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis) technique.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_007
nodes.label: Research Methodology
nodes.question: What method was utilized to conduct the literature review on AI applications for retrofit projects?
nodes.answer: The literature review was conducted using the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis) technique, which emphasizes systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized trials.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_008
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What methodology was employed in this study to assess AI applications for retrofit processes?
nodes.answer: The study used the PRISMA technique for systematic reviews and meta-analyses, combining qualitative systematic review and thematic analysis to assess literature on AI applications in retrofit processes from 2005 to 2023.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What methodologies were employed in the study to review literature on AI applications for retrofit processes?
nodes.answer: The study utilized a mixed-method literature review comprising a qualitative systematic review and a thematic analysis, incorporating the PRISMA technique for systematic documentation.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Smart cities|Energy management|Cognitive buildings for energy optimization_qna_010
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What challenge does the demand for computational power in AI development pose for smaller countries?
nodes.answer: Smaller countries may lack the infrastructure to support the growing energy demands of AI, raising concerns about their ability to participate in AI development at larger scales.
